sentences.text:
ORAL JUDGMENT : (KISHORE C. SANT, J.)
1. Rule.
Rule made returnable forthwith by consent of the parties.
2. Heard the parties.
3. The land of the petitioners is shown to be reserved for D.P. Road.
However, till now neither steps for acquisition are taken nor compensation is paid to the claimants.

When the petitioner No.1 sent notice under Section 127 of M.R.T.P. Act, the Municipal Corporation passed a resolution to initiate steps for payment of compensation and has taken steps for initiation of the acquisition proceeding.
However, subsequently the Corporation again passed a resolution resolving to give to the petitioner TDR in lieu of compensation.
However, no further steps are taken.

The petitioners are, therefore,
before this Court praying for expeditious completion of land acquisition proceeding.
4. The learned Advocate Shri Rane vehemently argued that the earlier resolution was passed by the Municipal Corporation clearly resolving to initiate land acquisition proceeding.
The subsequent resolution that was passed was rescinded by the State Government and therefore, it cannot in any case be considered.
He further submits that the TDR can be granted only where the owner of the property by ..3.. 907-WP-8159-17 mutual arrangement shows willingness to accept the same.
However, grant of TDR by Corporation cannot be an unilateral Act.
The Corporation can certainly offer TDR.
However, it cannot be force a person to accept the same.
Duty of the Corporation is to pay compensation.
He submits that at both the ends of this property the construction of road is already done.
The land was acquired for road purpose.
The land is only used as kaccha road since last 10-15 years and in such circumstances, it also is not possible to give back the land to the land owners.

5. He relies upon the Full Bench Judgment reported in 2022 (5) ABR 803 in the case of Shri Vinayak Builders and Developers Vs. State of Maharashtra and others, to submit that the writ petition be allowed by directing the authorities to initiate the acquisition proceedings.

entities.text: Shri Vinayak Builders and Developers Vs. State of Maharashtra and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 6. Learned Advocate Shri Gunale appearing for the Corporation, vehemently opposes the writ petition.
He submits that looking to the financial position of the corporation and upon objection raised by some of the corporators, the fresh resolution was passed by the Corporation.

As on today,
the corporation is not in a position to pay compensation.
In many pending cases, the land owners have accepted the TDR but only in this case the petitioners did not accept the TDR.
The TDR would in fact serve the purpose of the petitioners.

He also relies upon the judgment in the Writ Petition No. 10827 of 2017 of this Court in the case of Vinay Uttamchand Parakh Vs. The State of Maharashtra and others with other Writ Petition and he prays for dismissal of the petition.

sentences.text: This Court, thus, considered these submissions, we find that compensation need to be paid to the land owners.
It cannot be substituted with TDR unless it is mutually agreed by owners of the property and the Corporation.
In no case, the Corporation has approached this Court praying to direct the owners to accept the TDR.

9. This Court in the case of Vinayak (supra) has considered following three points :
"(i) Whether the modes of acquisition provided under Section 126(1)(a) and (b) of the Maharashtra Regional and Town Planning Act, 1966 are at the choice of either of the parties or only of the acquiring authority ?

entities.text: Maharashtra Regional and Town Planning Act, 1966
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
(ii) If the planning authority has approved the request of the landowner for grant of monetary compensation or grant of TDR/FSI in lieu of compensation, can the landowner withdraw his request and thereby refuse or decline to surrender the land ?
(iii) Can the grant of approval or passing of resolution by the authorities concerned for grant of TDR in lieu of monetary compensation be treated as a step for acquisition ..5.. 907-WP-8159-17 of land and thereby commencing the proceedings for acquisition of the land ?"
10.
The present case is covered under point No.(i) raised in the said petition.
It is clear that the owner needs to be compensated in terms of money when TDR is not acceptable to the owners.
11. Considering the above, this Court finds that the petition needs to be allowed.

It is, therefore,
allowed in terms of prayer clause 'A' which reads thus :
" The Hon'ble High Court may be pleased to issue appropriate writ, order or direction in the nature of writ and thereby direct the Respondents to complete the land acquisition proceedings expeditiously for acquisition of Gat No. 109/2 and part of 109/1 situated at Pimprala, District Jalgaon for the purpose of 30 Meters wide North-South D.P. Road."
12. Writ Petition stands disposed of.
13. No order as to costs.

14. Rule is made absolute in terms of prayer clause 'A'.
( SUSHIL M. GHODESWAR ) ( KISHORE C. SANT )
 JUDGE JUDGE shp/-
